readMe: Authored answer key. See PROVENANCE.md. `movable` is a human reading of the assumption, not a rerun of src/web/public-movable.ts.

positives.title: A background task can declare its own output path and have Monitor's read scope extended to exactly that path
positives.why: Whether Monitor's read restriction is a session-wide allowlist or a per-task grant is a property of the harness, and the harness documents its tools.

positives.title: A git merge driver can deterministically rebuild dist from source instead of needing a content-level diff merge
positives.why: Whether git invokes a merge driver with a usable toolchain, and what it guarantees about it, is in git's own manual.

positives.title: A narrow wait-for-condition primitive covers the polling shapes Monitor currently refuses
positives.why: Monitor's accepted grammar and its refusal conditions are published in its tool description.

positives.title: A postinstall step gets to run and speak on a stock setup
positives.why: Whether npm, pnpm and yarn run lifecycle scripts by default is documented and has changed in published release notes. The cleanest lookup in the tree.

positives.title: A probe spec can be kept out of the default vitest run and still run when named, using the argv check the config already applies to contended files
positives.why: Whether an `exclude` entry can be conditioned on argv is vitest's documented config behaviour.

positives.title: Editor tooling can auto-read a file transparently before a first Write Edit without weakening the guard's protection against blind overwrites
positives.why: Whether any editor integration already performs a transparent pre-read is a property of published editor plugins.

positives.title: Extent flags mostly point at real duplicates, not at distinct needs sharing a source
positives.why: FALSE POSITIVE. Matched Torres via a child test that re-judges flags 'against Torres's test'. The published method could settle the criterion, but the belief is about what this tree's own arithmetic emitted, which no outside document has seen.

positives.title: Inline code handed to tsx from the repo root resolves bare packages and . src paths the same way a checked-in file does
positives.why: Module resolution for `tsx -e` is tsx's documented behaviour.

positives.title: Most of what this loop waits on is work the harness tracks, not shell-backgrounded jobs it started itself
positives.why: FALSE POSITIVE. What the harness can track is public; what THIS loop mostly waits on is a distribution over this repository's own transcripts. The proposition is the distribution.

positives.title: Publishing Monitor's accepted grammar up front would cut the refusal-then-retry cost these transcripts show
positives.why: Whether the tool description already states those constraints is checkable against the published surface, and a yes would retire the candidate outright.

positives.title: The expiry convention can be bought on the machine the loop actually runs on
positives.why: Whether stock macOS ships timeout(1) — and what Homebrew's coreutils installs it as — is settled by public man pages and package listings.

positives.title: The harness can reliably tell created by this session apart from pre-existing, this session just wrote to it
positives.why: A property of the harness's file-state tracking, described in its published behaviour and its issue tracker.

positives.title: The harness can reliably tell which files this session itself created versus pre-existing files it hasn't read
positives.why: Same referent and same public source as the assumption above; the tree carries the belief twice.

positives.title: The harness exposes a hook at the moment a session is backgrounded or interrupted, in time to write one line before control is lost
positives.why: The set of lifecycle hooks a session exposes is documented; this is a lookup, not an experiment.

positives.title: The platform's own waiting forms are actually accepted on the unattended surface, where the bespoke helper was written to get around them
positives.why: Which waiting forms the surface accepts or refuses is stated by the surface itself, publicly.

positives.title: The scheduling harness can afford a fresh git worktree per firing without materially slowing the build loop or exhausting disk
positives.why: FALSE POSITIVE. Worktree cost in general is public; whether it is affordable turns on this loop's firing cadence and this machine's disk, which are ours.

positives.title: The set of built-ins a host can hand a pass is enumerable and stable enough to commit
positives.why: The built-in tool list and its churn are published; enumerability and stability are both readable off the vendor's own documentation and changelog.

negativeSample.why: A claim about what a buyer would do. Interviews move it; no document does.

negativeSample.title: A closed solution-kind disposition takes a solution off the instrument bucket and is disclosed on the response that withheld it
negativeSample.why: About this repository's own call sites.

negativeSample.why: About this product's own capability envelope.

negativeSample.title: A single fixed per-run friction-count threshold separates sessions worth the operator's attention from ordinary recoverable noise
negativeSample.why: About this operator's attention.

negativeSample.title: A trace of calls, outcomes and durations carries the defects a session actually had

negativeSample.title: An operator who must move the window by hand will actually move it more than once

negativeSample.title: Independent judges converge on the same riskiest assumption, so agreement means something
negativeSample.why: MISS. Inter-judge agreement between independent model judges is a published, measured question; the literature would raise or lower this belief before any local run does.

negativeSample.why: About this operator.

negativeSample.title: The stored measurements came from comparable enough conditions to be a distribution
negativeSample.why: About the provenance of measurements stored here.

negativeSample.title: Two practitioners place the same opportunity under the same sub-outcome
negativeSample.why: Needs two practitioners, not a document.

negativeSample.title: Without a controlling terminal the prompting tool fails loudly instead of silently taking its default
negativeSample.why: MISS. How a prompting CLI behaves with stdin closed and no controlling terminal is that tool's documented (or source-readable) behaviour. The classifier missed it because the belief names no vendor — 'the prompting tool' is a role, and a role has no documentation home.
